raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Non-streaming Kimi K3 content leaked raw XTML control-marker fragments when generation was cut mid-marker (`max_tokens`); the streaming path already kept them out of content, so the two paths returned different content for the same output. Gives `_strip_response_content` the streaming path's holdback and first-close boundary. Fixes #63941.

## Claims

- Non-streaming and streaming now parse every prefix of a K3 turn identically: the in-tree sweeps cover four turn shapes exhaustively (967 cut positions + 967 delta-split positions) — 174 divergent cut positions pre-fix, 0 post-fix, every divergence a raw marker fragment in content. The issue's parser-level scan over six turn shapes (1,525 conforming-family + 107 stray-control cut positions) found 235 pre-fix (216 + 19), 0 post-fix.
- No marker text reaches `content` on the truncation axis this PR fixes: the sweeps assert identical, marker-free `content` at every cut and delta-split position — the assert checks for `<|`, the common prefix of every XTML delimiter, so partial fragments like `<|clos` are caught too. The `message_close` family (model omits `response_close`) is a known residual, unchanged by this PR — see Details.
- No behavior change for complete (untruncated) conforming turns. Non-conforming complete outputs change by design toward streaming's boundary — e.g. body text sitting after a complete close is now dropped, matching what streaming already does.

## Validation

### Reproducer (from the issue)

`main`:

```
cut=25  ns='Just chatting, no tools.<'
cut=30  ns='Just chatting, no tools.<|clos'
cut=40  ns='Just chatting, no tools.<|close|>respons'
cut=60  ns='Just chatting, no tools.<|close|>mes'
```

this PR: `ns` returns `'Just chatting, no tools.'` at every cut, matching streaming.

### Tests

```
pytest tests/tool_use/test_kimi_k3_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_kimi_k3_named_tool_choice.py -q
→ 45 passed
```

The four new `test_truncated_output_parses_identically_in_both_paths[...]` cases fail with the parser from `main` and pass with this change:

```
git checkout main -- vllm/tool_parsers/kimi_k3_tool_parser.py
pytest tests/tool_use/test_kimi_k3_tool_parser.py -q
→ 4 failed, 37 passed
git checkout HEAD -- vllm/tool_parsers/kimi_k3_tool_parser.py
```

The sweep extends the existing suite: it drives both paths over every prefix cut (fresh parser per cut — each cut is an independent stream) and every two-delta split, asserting identical `(content, tool_calls)` and no `<|` in `content` — the common prefix of every XTML delimiter, so partial marker fragments are caught, not just complete markers.

No model evals were run: the change is a deterministic text transformation at the parser layer with no numerical component; the parity sweeps above are the validation.

### Duplicate check (re-run today)

No open or merged PR implements the non-streaming withhold this PR adds. Same class, not overlapping: #47903 (hermes truncation axis, open — different parser and file; this PR does not touch hermes). Same file, same marker, opposite direction, untouched by this PR: #51399/#51400 and #54273 — a complete `<|close|>message<|sep|>` leaking into **streamed** content when the model omits `response_close`; #51400 grows the streaming stop/hold set from three markers to four, and if it lands first this PR's mirrored three-marker set must follow in lockstep (no textual overlap — it edits `_extract_response_content`, this PR edits `_strip_response_content`). Competing direction, explicitly flagged: #60642 (open draft) flushes the withheld partial marker into `content` at stream EOF — the opposite resolution of the same divergence. It is streaming-side only and does not touch the non-streaming leak fixed here; the directions are mutually exclusive for mid-marker cuts with no complete close. This PR implements withhold (the direction #51400/#54273 propose for `message_close` and #47903 reports for hermes); if flush is preferred, the PR downscopes rather than drops — the holdback half is withdrawn, but the cap half stays: #60642's flush fires only when no complete marker caps the text, so cuts after a complete close (79 of the 235 divergent positions) still need the non-streaming cap (measured: a cap-only variant leaves 156 diffs, all no-complete-close cuts). Related but different: #63309/#63327 (stray `<tool_call>` in prose: hermes streaming content drop and its pending fix), #57353 (reasoning parser, think-channel truncation classification; open fixes #57366/#50291 stay in the think channel), #60655 (response transitions; explicitly excludes wrapper cleanup and tools-open handling), #62507 (merged 2026-10-22; request-layer `spaces_between_special_tokens` on the Responses API). The issue's secondary observation about the streaming path's literal-prefix holdback vs whitespace-tolerant regexes is documented there and deliberately not bundled here. #50627 (open, last updated 2026-09-13) also modifies this parser and its test file, but for a different problem — streaming tool-call argument granularity, not the truncation-axis content leak this PR fixes.

## Details

Root cause: the streaming path withholds a trailing partial control marker via `_partial_tag_overlap` (`_extract_response_content`); the non-streaming `_strip_response_content` had no equivalent, so a cut inside `<|close|>response<|sep|>`, `<|open|>tools<|sep|>` or the `<|close|>message<|sep|>` trailer stayed in `content` verbatim. Each marker is three tokens — two atomic delimiters plus the channel word (the delimiters are added tokens in Kimi K3's tokenizer, and `response`/`message`/`tools` are single BPE tokens) — so `max_tokens` cuts land inside them routinely.

Fix, in `_strip_response_content`:

- When no complete response close caps the text, trim a trailing partial marker with the same `_partial_tag_overlap` call and the same three-marker set (`response_open` / `response_close` / `tools_open`) the streaming path uses — parity by construction. A complete close keeps capping, so a body legitimately ending in `<` before a complete close is preserved exactly as streaming sends it.
- Cap at the first response close (`text[:m_close.start()]`) instead of stripping all occurrences and joining, which mirrors the streaming sendable boundary and stops trailer text after the close (e.g. a truncated `<|close|>message<|sep|>`) from leaking into content.
- Deliberately unchanged: `message_close` is not in the holdback set (neither path has it there). When a model omits `response_close` (reachable per #51399), a partial `<|close|>mes` trailer still surfaces in **both** paths identically — parity holds, the fragment still leaks — and the complete `<|close|>message<|sep|>` still leaks in **streaming** only (#51399/#54273, fix #51400 open). Adding `message_close` to one path alone would recreate the divergence in the opposite direction; this PR's mirrored set follows #51400 in lockstep.

Tradeoff: a body whose final character is a marker prefix (e.g. `… 5 <`) and whose generation ends exactly there is now withheld in non-streaming too — identical to what streaming already does, so the paths agree. The open draft #60642 flushes that same withheld tail at stream EOF instead (every character kept, raw marker text in `content`); the directions are mutually exclusive for mid-marker cuts with no complete close, so whichever wins should win on both paths — withhold implemented here per #51400/#54273/#47903's framing, maintainer's call.

---

<summary>Pull Request Checklist</summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Model-specific fix inside `kimi_k3_tool_parser.py` per `vllm/tool_parsers/AGENTS.md`; reuses `_partial_tag_overlap`; +23/−5 lines in one method.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Regression tests shown failing without the fix and passing with it; runs in existing CPU-only CI suite (no tokenizer downloads — stub tokenizer, matching the file's existing pattern).
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** ruff 0.14.0 (the version `.pre-commit-config.yaml` pins), run on both changed files from the repo root: `ruff check` → `All checks passed!`, `ruff format --check` → `2 files already formatted`; comments limited to the non-obvious decisions (cap-at-first-close, holdback, partial-fragment assert).
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Summary, evidence, root cause, tradeoffs and duplicate-check conclusion included.
</details>

files.patch:
@@ -25,6 +25,7 @@
 THINK_OPEN = f"{OPEN}think{SEP}"
 THINK_CLOSE = f"{CLOSE}think{SEP}"
 RESPONSE_CLOSE = f"{CLOSE}response{SEP}"
+MESSAGE_CLOSE = f"{CLOSE}message{SEP}"
 
 
 class DummyTokenizer:
@@ -714,3 +715,138 @@ def test_chat_params_keeps_template_tool_choice_when_api_auto():
 
     assert chat_params.chat_template_kwargs["tool_choice"] == "required"
     assert chat_params.tool_choice == "auto"
+
+
+def _stream_deltas(
+    parser: KimiK3ToolParser, deltas: list[str]
+) -> tuple[str | None, list[tuple[str | None, str]]]:
+    """Feed deltas through the streaming path and accumulate the result."""
+    request = _request()
+    previous_text = ""
+    messages: list[DeltaMessage] = []
+    for i, delta in enumerate(deltas, start=1):
+        current_text = previous_text + delta
+        message = parser.extract_tool_calls_streaming(
+            previous_text=previous_text,
+            current_text=current_text,
+            delta_text=delta,
+            previous_token_ids=[],
+            current_token_ids=[i],
+            delta_token_ids=[i],
+            request=request,
+        )
+        if message is not None:
+            messages.append(message)
+        previous_text = current_text
+    content = "".join(message.content or "" for message in messages) or None
+    calls: list[tuple[str | None, str]] = []
+    for message in messages:
+        for tool_call in message.tool_calls or []:
+            assert tool_call.function is not None
+            calls.append((tool_call.function.name, tool_call.function.arguments or ""))
+    return content, calls
+
+
+def _extracted(
+    parser: KimiK3ToolParser, output: str
+) -> tuple[str | None, list[tuple[str | None, str]]]:
+    extracted = parser.extract_tool_calls(output, _request())
+    return extracted.content, [
+        (tool_call.function.name, tool_call.function.arguments)
+        for tool_call in extracted.tool_calls
+    ]
+
+
+# Realistic XTML assistant turns: the message close trailer is generated by
+# the model on every turn, and the response open marker is only generated in
+# thinking mode (otherwise it stays in the prompt prefix).
+_PARITY_OUTPUTS = {
+    "prefix_consumed": (
+        "Let me check the weather."
+        + RESPONSE_CLOSE
+        + _tools(_call("get_weather", 1, _arg("city", "string", "Paris")))
+        + MESSAGE_CLOSE
+    ),
+    "response_open": (
+        _response("Checking.")
+        + _tools(_call("run_query", 1, _arg("opts", "object", '{"a": 1}')))
+        + MESSAGE_CLOSE
+    ),
+    "two_calls": (
+        "First."
+        + RESPONSE_CLOSE
+        + _tools(
+            _call("f1", 1, _arg("text", "string", "line1\nline2")),
+            _call("f2", 2, _arg("n", "number", "3.14")),
+        )
+        + MESSAGE_CLOSE
+    ),
+    "no_tools": "Just chatting, no tools." + RESPONSE_CLOSE + MESSAGE_CLOSE,
+}
+
+
+def test_object_argument_is_json_decoded():
+    parser = KimiK3ToolParser(_dummy_tokenizer())
+
+    output = _response("Checking.") + _tools(
+        _call("run_query", 1, _arg("opts", "object", '{"a": 1, "b": [true, null]}'))
+    )
+    _, calls = _extracted(parser, output)
+
+    assert calls == [("run_query", json.dumps({"opts": {"a": 1, "b": [True, None]}}))]
+
+
+def test_empty_and_missing_arguments():
+    parser = KimiK3ToolParser(_dummy_tokenizer())
+
+    output = _tools(
+        _call("edge", 1, _arg("s", "string", ""), _arg("empty", "object", "{}")),
+        _call("noargs", 2),
+    )
+    _, calls = _extracted(parser, output)
+
+    assert [name for name, _ in calls] == ["edge", "noargs"]
+    assert json.loads(calls[0][1]) == {"s": "", "empty": {}}
+    assert json.loads(calls[1][1]) == {}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", list(_PARITY_OUTPUTS))
+def test_streaming_char_deltas_match_non_streaming(name):
+    output = _PARITY_OUTPUTS[name]
+    parser = KimiK3ToolParser(_dummy_tokenizer())
+
+    assert _stream_deltas(parser, list(output)) == _extracted(parser, output)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", list(_PARITY_OUTPUTS))
+def test_truncated_output_parses_identically_in_both_paths(name):
+    """Every prefix cut (e.g. max_tokens) must parse identically in both
+    paths, and raw control markers must never surface in content."""
+    output = _PARITY_OUTPUTS[name]
+    for cut in range(len(output) + 1):
+        prefix = output[:cut]
+        expected = _extracted(KimiK3ToolParser(_dummy_tokenizer()), prefix)
+        assert (
+            _stream_deltas(KimiK3ToolParser(_dummy_tokenizer()), list(prefix))
+            == expected
+        ), f"cut at {cut}"
+        # "<|" prefixes every XTML delimiter, so this also catches
+        # partial fragments (e.g. "<|clos") a full-marker check misses.
+        assert "<|" not in (expected[0] or ""), f"marker leak at cut {cut}"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", list(_PARITY_OUTPUTS))
+def test_arbitrary_delta_split_parses_identically(name):
+    """Splitting the full output at any delta boundary must not change the
+    result."""
+    output = _PARITY_OUTPUTS[name]
+    expected = _extracted(KimiK3ToolParser(_dummy_tokenizer()), output)
+    assert "<|" not in (expected[0] or "")
+    for split in range(len(output) + 1):
+        assert (
+            _stream_deltas(
+                KimiK3ToolParser(_dummy_tokenizer()),
+                [output[:split], output[split:]],
+            )
+            == expected
+        ), f"split at {split}"

@@ -259,13 +259,31 @@ def _strip_response_content(self, text: str) -> str | None:
         m_open = self._response_open_re.search(text)
         if m_open is not None:
             m_close = self._response_close_re.search(text, m_open.end())
-            if m_close is not None:
-                text = text[m_open.end() : m_close.start()]
-            else:
-                text = text[m_open.end() :]
+            text = (
+                text[m_open.end() : m_close.start()]
+                if m_close is not None
+                else text[m_open.end() :]
+            )
         else:
-            text = self._response_close_re.sub("", text)
+            m_close = self._response_close_re.search(text)
+            if m_close is not None:
+                # cap at the first close like the streaming path: anything
+                # after it (e.g. a <|close|>message<|sep|> trailer) is not
+                # response content
+                text = text[: m_close.start()]
         text = self._message_close_re.sub("", text)
+        if m_close is None:
+            # Nothing caps the text, so its tail may be a control-marker
+            # fragment from a stream cut mid-marker (e.g. max_tokens).
+            # Withhold it exactly like the streaming path's overlap holdback
+            # so raw markers never leak into content.
+            overlap = max(
+                _partial_tag_overlap(text, self.response_open),
+                _partial_tag_overlap(text, self.response_close),
+                _partial_tag_overlap(text, self.tools_open),
+            )
+            if overlap:
+                text = text[: len(text) - overlap]
         return text or None
 
     def _content(self, model_output: str, before: str) -> str | None:
